maths_side.label: theorems in mathlib, across 34 subject areas
maths_side.source: deck/FACTS.md §1.2 — leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib_stats.html, Counts table: 140,094 definitions / 292,237 theorems / 772 contributors.
maths_side.do_not_say: Never “292,237 distinct mathematical results” (many are auto-generated simp/instance lemmas) and never “proved by AI” (mathlib is overwhelmingly human-written).

biology_side.label: not one of those 34 subject areas is biology
biology_side.source: deck/FACTS.md §2.3, the only clean zero this project owns: zero of mathlib’s 34 subject areas.
biology_side.do_not_say: Never a bare “0 novel proven biology theorems”, never “nobody has done biology in a proof assistant”, never “we are the first to formalise biology in Lean”, and never the word zero without saying zero OF WHAT. A Lean formalisation of the central dogma was posted 2026-10-26 (arXiv:2610.36343), so a bare zero is refutable from memory.

attrition.sentence: Nine in ten drug programmes that enter Phase 1 never get approved.
attrition.long: Between 86 and 92 percent of drug programmes that enter Phase 1 never reach approval.
sources: BIO / Informa / QLS, 2011-2020: 12,728 phase transitions across 9,704 programmes; 7.9% of Phase 1 programmes reach approval
Wong, Siah & Lo, Biostatistics 2019 (MIT): 185,994 trials, 21,143 compounds; 13.8%
attrition.source: deck/FACTS.md 3.4, the exact sentence that section permits.
attrition.do_not_say: Never “90% of clinical trials fail” — the unit is the PROGRAMME, not the trial. Never “86-92% of drugs fail” without “entering Phase 1”: the figure is conditional on reaching Phase 1 and says nothing about preclinical attrition. Never average 7.9% and 13.8% into one number: different datasets, windows and unit definitions, so give both or give one.

swarm_benchmark.design: n = 3 tasks per (arm, stage) · 36 cells · 113 logged calls · $8.35 list price
swarm_benchmark.prereg: swarm/benchmark/ARMS.md, written before the first call
swarm_benchmark.source_file: swarm/benchmark/RESULTS.md and results.json; raw logs one JSON per cell under dashboard/public/t/benchmark/logs/
swarm_benchmark.stage_shown: Stage 4, validation-framework use — RESULTS.md calls it “the cleanest cell of the benchmark and the one that was expected to discriminate most. It did not.”
swarm_benchmark.headline: Quality did not separate. Neither did honesty.
swarm_benchmark.result_line: All three arms met the same trap case — nothing failed, four results cannot-assess, composite 0.8449 flagged “plausible”. All three refused to call it a pass. The largest quality gap, 0.048, sits inside the 0.143 spread. Across the three stages shown, the swarms cost 1.5x to 4.0x the single agent.
swarm_benchmark.caveats: n = 3, single draws, no replicates · no arm had tools, so this measures reasoning architectures, not tool coordination — and ours is tool-coordinated.
not_shown: Stage 3 (design studio) quality AND its cost ratio. RESULTS.md §6 records that the task briefs were infeasible at the current lawset, so “accepted” was unreachable by construction. Its 5.94x cost ratio is excluded for the same reason the quality is: a defective task cannot grade an architecture, and a ratio cannot be quoted out of a stage whose result is suppressed.

The centralised arm’s stage-1 zero. What the logs support: the arm produced no artifact in 3 of 3 cells, 8 of its 18 calls hit the $0.09 per-call cap, and a post-hoc re-allocation of the same total produced an artifact in 3 of 3. The cap starved the arm at the join. The per-call logs do not record a call’s ROLE, so no call can be shown to be the merge and no dollar figure is attributed to a named merge attempt. Nothing here says the workers’ drafts graded better than any other arm’s artifact — the candidate grades show parses 0 and parses_valid_rdf 0, the same as the other arms. Shown without its rescue the zero reads as “centralisation does not pay”, which is false, and both halves will not fit legibly in eight seconds.
swarm_benchmark.no_result_line: Pre-registered before the first call. 3 architectures x 4 stages x 3 tasks, every run logged. At n = 3 we claim no winner.

cost_range.note: Taken per (stage, arm) from results.json and recomputed here, over the three stages the film shows. The 5.94x that appears in RESULTS.md’s own headline range comes from the DESIGN stage, which this film omits because its task briefs were infeasible by construction. Quoting a ratio while suppressing the stage it came from is the move this film exists to refuse, so the range stops at 4.0x.

swarm_benchmark.calls_note: 113 is the number of call records the log files contain, counted here across all 36 cells. RESULTS.md’s header says 108, which is the nominal 12 + 36 + 60; the extra five are retries in two decentralised and three centralised cells. The film says “logged calls” and uses 113, the number a viewer could check against dashboard/public/t/benchmark/logs/.
